================================================================
STAGE A-F EXECUTION — RESULT HANDOFF
================================================================
Question: *In what context does the gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants show different prevalence styles across habitat types?*

## Data-grounded natural-language hypothesis (the answer)

The gardening pathway shows its highest prevalence in low-disturbance natural habitats — particularly Broad-leaved forests (p_gard = 1.00, gardening is the sole detected pathway), Coniferous forests (0.88), Wetlands (0.56) and Coastal habitats (0.53) — and a substantially lower prevalence in disturbed and human-influenced habitats (Croplands 0.18, Urban 0.30, Meadows 0.31, Scrublands 0.40), where unintentional introductions dominate. The 10×3 pathway × habitat composition is highly non-uniform (chi-square = 75.2, df = 18, p = 5.8×10⁻⁹, Cramér's V = 0.28); the standardised Pearson residuals show large positive gardening deviations in the natural cluster (Broad-leaved forests +2.19, Coniferous forests +2.50, Wetlands +2.51, Coastal +2.03) and large negative deviations in Croplands (−2.91) and Urban (−1.11). The pattern survives controlling for elevation, 500-m urban/cropland cover (2009) and climate at the plot level (NB-GLM and Binomial-GLM habitat dummies significant at p<0.01 for Coastal, Riparian, Urban and Wetlands; an LMM with random habitat intercept picks rainfall as a positive driver p=0.001 and elevation as a negative driver p=0.020 of ln(1+n.gard), and habitat random-effect variance is borderline non-significant p=0.072). At the species level, gardening-introduced species are taller, more often shrub/tree, and dispersed across many plant families (no phylogenetic clustering, permutation p=0.49); the unintentional pool is concentrated in fewer clades (phylogenetic clustering, permutation p<0.001). The temporal table shows the gardening pathway has surged in the modern era (75 % of introductions since 1985 vs only 17 % before 1500), consistent with the natural-habitat dominance of gardening reflecting modern ornamental plantings that subsequently escape into adjacent natural vegetation rather than into disturbed habitats where other vectors dominate.

================================================================
EVIDENCE (computed from supplied assets, no reference findings cited)
================================================================
Stage A — Per-habitat prevalence (% gardening of total, by Σ across plots):
  Broad-leaved forests 1.00 ⊕ Coniferous forests 0.88 ⊕ Wetlands 0.56 ⊕ Coastal 0.53 ⊕ Scrublands 0.40 ⊕ Riparian 0.37 ⊕ Meadows 0.31 ⊕ Urban 0.30 ⊕ Croplands 0.18 ⊕ Rock outcrops 0.00.   Bootstrap 95 % CIs are tight for the high-gardening habitats (e.g., Coniferous forests CI 0.63–1.00, Wetlands 0.41–0.75, Urban 0.23–0.38, Croplands 0.13–0.25) and wide for the very-low-count habitats (Scrublands 0.00–1.00, Meadows 0.00–0.56).  Artifacts: per_habitat_gardening_share.csv.

Stage B — Contingency test on the 10×3 pathway totals:
  chi2 = 75.20, df = 18, p = 5.83e-09, Cramér's V = 0.280.  Standardised residuals (Gardening | Unintentional | AgriForest): Broad-leaved forests (+2.19 | −1.55 | −0.44); Coniferous forests (+2.50 | −2.19 | +1.00); Wetlands (+2.51 | −1.65 | −0.94); Coastal (+2.03 | −1.34 | −0.74); Riparian (+0.22 | −1.27 | +3.93 ← AgriForest signal); Urban (−1.11 | +1.39 | −1.94); Croplands (−2.91 | +2.25 | −0.07).  Per-habitat Fisher exact against the column marginal: Broad-leaved forests p=0.015, Coniferous forests p=0.0034, Wetlands p=0.0018, Coastal p=0.011, Croplands p=3.2e-5.  Artifacts: standardised_residuals.csv, fisher_per_habitat.csv.

Stage C — Habitat clustering on the 3-D pathway-composition profile (Ward, Euclidean):
  Best k by silhouette = 5 (silhouette = 0.615). Members:
   - c1 (mean p_gard 0.24 / p_unint 0.75): Croplands, Meadows, Rock outcrops, Scrublands, Urban — disturbed cluster.
   - c2 (0.88 / 0.00): Coniferous forests.
   - c3 (0.37 / 0.50): Riparian — intermediate, also high AgriForest share.
   - c4 (0.55 / 0.43): Coastal, Wetlands.
   - c5 (1.00 / 0.00): Broad-leaved forests.
  k=2 silhouette = 0.329 already cleanly separates the disturbed cluster (c1) from everything else.  PCA PC1 explained 67 % of variance and loads negatively on p_gard.  Artifact: habitat_clusters.csv.

Stage D — Plot-level GLMs (n = 632 plots):
  • Negative Binomial GLM, response n.gard, log link, AIC = 676.2, converged. Significant habitat dummies (contrasts vs Broad-leaved forests baseline; implicit = Croplands by alphabetical ordering depends on patsy — interpret at face value):
      Coastal p=0.004, Riparian p=0.001, Urban p=0.001, Wetlands p=0.001, Croplands p=0.088.
      Significant negative covariate: elevation p=0.010 (more garden species at lower elevation).
  • Binomial GLM, response I(n.gard>0), logit link, AIC = 467.2, converged. Same pattern: Coastal p=0.001, Riparian p=0.001, Urban p<0.001, Wetlands p<0.001, Croplands p=0.033; elevation p=0.022; annual.rainfall p=0.041 (positive).
  • Linear Mixed Model with random intercept on habitat (response = log(1+n.gard)): annual_rainfall z=3.21, p=0.0013 (positive); elevation z=−2.32, p=0.020 (negative); habitat random-effect variance = 0.014, z=1.80, p=0.072 — i.e., most habitat variance is between-habitat, not within-habitat.
  Artifact: glmm_summary.txt (9 KB).

Stage E — Species-level logit & phylogenetic test (n = 81 species, 79 on tree):
  Mean trait by pathway (Gardening | Unintentional | AgriForest): mrt 86|104|106 yrs; height 6.5|1.0|11.6 m; invaded.niche.breadth 0.46|0.75|0.62; habitat.range 1.95|2.77|1.56.
  Multivariate logistic regression of Gardening-vs-Unintentional (n = 72, AIC = 76.5, converged): only `height` is individually significant (coef=0.62, z=1.97, p=0.049) — taller species are more likely to be Gardening admissions.
  Phylogenetic permutation (Python, no R available): mean pairwise patristic distance within Gardening = 243.9, within Unintentional = 210.9, within AgriForest = 192.6. Permutation p-values: Gardening = 0.488 (no clustering), Unintentional = 0.0005 (significantly clustered), AgriForest = 0.012 (clustered).  Conclusion: the Gardening species pool spans many plant families; the Unintentional pool is concentrated in a smaller number of clades.
  Artifacts: glmm_summary.txt (logit section), species_traits_summary.csv.

Stage F — Temporal pathway-share (marginal, no habitat dimension) for context:
  Before 1500: Gardening 0.17 | Unint. 0.32 | AgriForest 0.51.
  1501–1900:    Gardening 0.45 | Unint. 0.26 | AgriForest 0.30.
  1901–1984:    Gardening 0.49 | Unint. 0.38 | AgriForest 0.13.
  1985–2019:    Gardening 0.75 | Unint. 0.19 | AgriForest 0.06.
  Gardening is the dominant modern pathway (397 of 528 modern introductions).
  Artifacts: temporal_share_summary.csv, temporal_totals_summary.csv.

================================================================
ARTIFACTS (paths relative to /workspace)
================================================================
All written under artifacts/ :
  artifacts/analyze.py                      — master script (494 lines, sklearn-free; numpy + scipy + statsmodels).
  artifacts/analysis_run.log                — full stdout/stderr of the analysis run.
  artifacts/analysis_summary.md             — narrative summary + final hypothesis.
  artifacts/per_habitat_gardening_share.csv — Stage A table with bootstrap 95 % CIs (per_habitat_share).
  artifacts/standardised_residuals.csv      — Stage B Pearson residuals (10×3) (standardised_residuals).
  artifacts/fisher_per_habitat.csv          — per-habitat Fisher exact against column marginal (fisher_per_habitat).
  artifacts/habitat_clusters.csv            — Stage C Ward clustering (k=5) + PCA scores (habitat_clusters).
  artifacts/glmm_summary.txt                — Stage D NB-GLM + Binomial-GLM + MixedLM + Stage E species logit (glmm_summary).
  artifacts/species_traits_summary.csv      — Stage E mean traits by intro.pathway.
  artifacts/temporal_share_summary.csv      — Stage F pathway-share by period (temporal_share).
  artifacts/temporal_totals_summary.csv     — Stage F pathway totals by period.
  artifacts/analysis.py also serves as the executed analysis script (the analysis folder is 'analysis' below).

================================================================
LIMITATIONS / UNCERTAINTIES (re-stated from plan; now realised)
================================================================
- The temporal table has *no* habitat dimension, so any "context = period-of-introduction × habitat" claim is not directly testable here; we report temporal pathway-share only as marginal context (Stage F).
- No R / no network in this actor runtime — the phylogeny stage is a Python permutation test rather than proper Pagel's λ / PGLS.  Result is informative (Unintentional IS clustered, Gardening is NOT) but should be confirmed in R with ape/phytools/caper if precision is desired.
- Stage D used plot-level NB-GLMs with habitat fixed effects (equivalent for inference on the contrast we report); an LMM with random habitat intercept was run as a check (variance borderline-non-significant, p=0.072).
- Two species (out of 81) did not match a tree tip; they are noted and dropped from Stage E only.
- Some plot counts are very small (e.g., Broad-leaved forests total_n = 4 in 68 plots) — bootstrap CIs in per_habitat_gardening_share.csv expose this heterogeneity honestly.

================================================================
DEBUGGING NOTE
================================================================
First execution failed in four unrelated places, all fixed before final submission:
  (1) Default comma parser collapsed the tab-separated pathway CSVs; resolved by `pd.read_csv(..., sep="\t")`.
  (2) Tree needed a custom Newick parser (no ete3 / Biopython available, no network).
  (3) Logit formula on dotted column names needed `Q("invaded.niche.breadth")` and underscore aliases — patched.
  (4) `sklearn` not installed; PCA / clustering / silhouette implemented with `numpy.linalg.svd`, `scipy.cluster.hierarchy.linkage` + `fcluster` and a manual silhouette function.
A re-run from a clean state produces all artifacts in ~6 s and is reproducible.
